found.desc: Llanbeblig. This medieval church is dedicated to Peblig, a 5thC saint, who according to legend was the son of Macsen Wledig (the Roman Emperor Magnus Maximus) whose wife Helen was a local girl. A disciple of St Martin of Tours, Peblig returned to the area and established a monastic settlement - (a 'llan')- on this site.

found.title: File:Summit of Mynydd Myddfai - geograph.org.uk - 842402.jpg
found.desc: Summit of Mynydd Myddfai The summit is decorated with a trig point, a toppled concrete pillar bearing the letters 'WD' and a more recent feature the temporary fencing running either side of the wide strip down which a major gas pipeline was laid in 2007. The enclosed area has been revegetated - largely successfully it would seem but needs to become properly re-established before being opened to grazing animals.

found.title: File:Tilestones diggings on Mynydd Myddfai - geograph.org.uk - 842379.jpg
found.desc: Tilestones diggings on Mynydd Myddfai The line of grassy pits can be traced for a long distance over the hilltop. A couple of geological faults offset the line of the Tilestones Formation south-east of Craig Cwm-clyd - the offsets are visible on the ground and the larger of the two can be seen on the OS 25K map too.
